_comment: Recruitment tuning, kept separate from data/races.json (which is the roster itself) because these are the knobs you retune during playtesting, not facts about a race. Loaded by RaceCatalog alongside races.json; read by RecruitGenerator. Implements FOUNDATION_SPEC section 3 (recruit generation) and RACES.md's 'power attracts power' rule.
_comment_power_tiers: The 'power attracts power' ladder from RACES.md: as settlement Power grows, recruit offers weight toward Uncommon/Rare. This is a TABLE, not a chain of if-statements in GDScript, so adding a fourth tier or retuning a weight is a JSON edit. Evaluated by picking the LAST entry whose min_power is <= current Power, so entries must stay sorted ascending by min_power. Weight keys must match the 'rarity' values in races.json exactly.
_comment_roll: FOUNDATION_SPEC section 3: value = clamp(baseline + d3 - d3, 1, 10). Two dice give a centre-weighted spread -- most recruits sit at baseline and +/-2 is rare, so 'some ogres are just stronger than others' without wild outliers.
_comment_exceptional: 5% chance per recruit of +1 to their category-defining stat after the roll. 'best_labor' means whichever of woodcutting/mining/foraging rolled highest for that individual -- an Economy race's defining trait is that it is good at *its* speciality, which varies by race (Gray Dwarf mines, Minotaur does both). 'none' means the category has no defining stat and never rolls exceptional: Versatile is the flat-5 jack-of-all-trades by definition, and Labor is the interchangeable-by-design Skeleton Worker.
_comment_first_run: GAME_OUTLINE Stage 3: a first-time run is guaranteed offers spanning the categories so new players see the full scope. These three categories are dealt, in order, as the first three offers; after that offers are pure weighted-random. 'Versatile' is deliberately absent -- RACES.md says Human Outcast 'counts as nothing for the first-run category guarantee'.
